chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved in a single Body?
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly institutional/pastoral (catechumen discipline, fasting, alms, church protection, merit accounting) wrapped in dialogue frame. The only recoverable older substrate consists of brief, more impersonal eschatological mechanism statements about post-mortem ascent and purification (firmaments/heavens; purification; ‘light image’; land of rest). There is explicit Christian overlay via a Pauline citation (¶4) and a likely Matthean proverb echo embedded in an otherwise mechanistic sequence (¶20).

paragraphs.core_text: when he comes out from his body, his soul shall [... ...] in the firmaments above, and he travels to the place of rest.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue-frame attribution (“Once again that elect speaks to this apostle:”) and the catechumen-specific setup leading into it; retained only the impersonal eschatological statement about exit from the body and travel through the firmaments to rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula and catechumen topic mark later compilation context, but the clause on post-mortem passage through firmaments to a ‘place of rest’ reads like a freestanding cosmological-eschatological mechanism that could predate the catechumenate application.
Direct petition/Q&A frame (“Now I beseech you, my master… instruct me…”) plus audience-management (“my other brothers”) is editorial container language.

Although introduced by a dialogue tag, the substance is a behavioral archetype for ‘perfect catechumens’ (marriage, property, relatives, ‘holy church’)—cosmos→institution/ethics rather than cosmos→cosmos.

Explicit ‘saviour… apostle’ citation of 1 Corinthians 7 language (“let these who have wives be like…”) indicates New Testament entry vector (Christian overlay), despite moral/ascetical fit with Manichaean practice.

Seam-like recap applying the preceding material to catechumen institutional categories (“perfect catechumens… like the elect… sign…”) functions as editorial consolidation/extension; not part of the older substrate.

Institutional discipline list (fasting, prayer, alms, ‘holy church’, ‘elect’, wife/children) and moral psychology (“potential for evil-doing is dead”) are pastoral catechesis, not systematic cosmology.
Exhortative identification (“Behold, this is the sign…”) plus reference to an authored book (“Treasure of Life”) and catechumen category are institutional/authorial, not substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: When, however, they come forth from their body, they travel on their way and pass by in the place above, and go in to the life. They shall be purified in the heavens, and they are plucked just as a fruit that ripens is plucked from the tree.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional application comparing purification to alms-offerings ‘that pass over to the elect’ and the explicit catechumen identification (“souls of the catechumens… resemble (the alms)”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening sentences describe a general post-mortem ascent/purification process in cosmic terms (above/heavens/life) with a natural correspondence (fruit plucked when ripe). The paragraph then pivots to church practice (alms to elect), a later application layer.
Authorial cross-reference (“I have written down in the Treasure of Life”) and merit-by-contribution-to-church framing are institutional.
Prescriptive instruction and ecclesial mediation (“pray… forgiveness… from God and the holy church”; ‘deeds… added to his account’) are pastoral/legal accounting.
Hagiographic closure: disciples praise/bless the teacher, laud his revelation to elect/catechumens, and use staircase imagery in a doxological register.
Renewed beseeching Q&A frame introducing a new topic (prior sins before joining the church); catalog of vices functions as question setup rather than substrate mechanism.

Though it uses Manichaean cosmological vocabulary (‘separated the light from the darkness’, ‘living soul’), the structure is sacramental/institutional (receiving ‘right hand of peace’ from the Light Mind ‘who dwells in the holy church’; asking forgiveness), consistent with later church practice framing.
Absolution doctrine is stated conditionally on persistence in belief; oriented to church-entry and renunciation of sects/idols—moral/juridical rather than cosmological mechanics.
Backsliding warning and repentance logic, explicitly keyed to catechumen/elect states, is disciplinary exhortation.
Brief institutional promise of absolution through fasting/prayer/alms—pastoral economy.
Detailed calendrical rule (fifty fasts on lord’s days; sexual restraint; dietary prohibitions; non-violence to ‘living soul’) is catechumen discipline.
Hours of prayer, alms, garment for saints, ‘daily communion’ and merit bookkeeping (‘half… for the good, the other half for sins’) are institutional practice.

Merit arithmetic (‘sins… separated into five parts’; church protection absolves four) and reliance on ‘holy church’/elect love dominate; cosmological phrases serve as justificatory rhetoric within the institutional scheme.

paragraphs.core_text: Afterwards he is purified, whether indeed above or below. He shall be purified according to the worth of his deeds, and cleansed and washed and adorned. Afterwards, he is sculpted a light image; and [he glid]es up and reaches the land of rest,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the opening merit-accounting and punishment clause (“As for the rest… questioned… receive blows… retribution.”) and removed the concluding proverb about heart/treasure (likely NT/Matthean echo). Retained the impersonal purification-to-transformation mechanism (‘light image’ → ascent → land of rest).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Middle of the paragraph shifts into a mechanistic eschatology (purification above/below; transformation into a ‘light image’; ascent to rest) consistent with older cosmological teaching; the surrounding moral accounting and the heart/treasure saying reflect later pastoral/Christianized framing.
Conditional recompense statement tied to steadfastness in catechumenate—disciplinary summary.
Moral warning about lying/apostasy and renewed total accounting of sins—pastoral admonition.
Salvation assurance is framed as conditional exhortation (‘if… steadfast…’) rather than cosmological exposition; no systematic internal mapping.

Closing hagiographic reaction formula (disciples glorify teacher). The added cosmological phrase (‘first light… through the Mind… riches of its knowledge’) functions as doxological ornament inside the frame, not standalone substrate teaching.
